eos.d: the winged goddess of the dawn in ancient mythology; daughter of Hyperion

eocene.d: from 58 million to 40 million years ago; presence of modern mammals

eon.d: a divine power or nature emanating from the Supreme Being and playing various roles in the operation of the universe

eohippus.d: earliest horse; extinct primitive dog-sized four-toed Eocene animal

eolian.d: a member of one of four linguistic divisions of the prehistoric Greeks

eosin.d: a red fluorescent dye resulting from the action of bromine on fluorescein; used in cosmetics and as a biological stain for studying cell structures

eosinopenia.d: a decrease in the number of eosinophils in the blood

eosinophil.d: a leukocyte readily stained with eosin

eolotropic.d: having properties with different values along different axes

eosinophilia.d: a symptom of allergic states; increased eosinophils in the blood

eosinophile.d: a leukocyte readily stained with eosin

eolithic.d: of or relating to the earliest period of the Stone Age (characterized by the use of eoliths)

eolith.d: a crude stone artifact (as a chipped flint); possibly the earliest tools
